pharm: Inotrope / vasodilator for acute heart failure
quick: Loading 50 mcg/kg IV over 10 min, then 0.375-0.75 mcg/kg/min infusion
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Unknown if excreted in milk; use with caution
Reduce infusion rate in renal impairment (drug accumulates)
Continuous ECG, BP, heart rate, fluid/electrolytes, renal function
summary: Milrinone is an intravenous phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor used for the short-term treatment of acute decompensated heart failure. By increasing intracellular cyclic AMP it produces positive inotropy and peripheral and pulmonary vasodilation (an 'inodilator'), raising cardiac output and lowering filling pressures. It must be given with continuous hemodynamic and ECG monitoring because of the risk of hypotension and ventricular arrhythmias, and the infusion rate is reduced in renal impairment.
indications: Short-term intravenous treatment of patients with acute decompensated heart failure

dosage.n: Administer slowly; may be omitted if hypotension feared
Titrate to hemodynamic response; standard 0.50 mcg/kg/min

dosage.d: Reduced infusion rate (e.g., 0.20-0.43 mcg/kg/min per CrCl)
dosage.n: Lower rate as creatinine clearance falls to avoid accumulation

admin: For intravenous use only after dilution in compatible fluid (e.g., normal saline or dextrose)
Give the loading dose slowly over 10 minutes to reduce hypotension
Administer via infusion pump with continuous hemodynamic monitoring
Do not mix with furosemide in the same line (precipitation)
Correct hypokalemia and hypovolemia before/during therapy
moa: Milrinone selectively inhibits the peak-III cyclic-AMP phosphodiesterase isoenzyme (PDE-3) in cardiac and vascular smooth muscle. The resulting rise in intracellular cyclic AMP increases calcium influx and contractility (positive inotropy) in myocardium and causes relaxation (vasodilation) of arterial and venous smooth muscle. The net effect is increased cardiac output with reduced preload and afterload, independent of beta-adrenergic stimulation.

relative: Severe aortic or pulmonic valvular obstruction (avoid - inotrope unhelpful)
monitor: Fluid status, electrolytes (especially potassium), and renal function

preg: There are no adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Milrinone should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether milrinone is excreted in human milk. Caution should be exercised when administered to a breastfeeding woman; given acute critical-care use, breastfeeding is usually interrupted.
renal: Milrinone is excreted largely unchanged in the urine, so renal impairment markedly prolongs its half-life and increases plasma levels. Reduce the maintenance infusion rate according to creatinine clearance to prevent accumulation and toxicity.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is generally recommended for hepatic impairment, as elimination is predominantly renal.

major: Furosemide - precipitates when mixed with milrinone in the same IV line; use separate lines
moderate: Other inotropes/vasodilators (additive hemodynamic effects - titrate carefully)
Diuretics (excessive volume depletion can cause hypotension)
minor: Drugs lowering potassium (increase arrhythmia risk via hypokalemia)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor potassium, renal function, and ECG; arrhythmias and hypokalemia may occur

serious: Increased ventricular response in atrial flutter/fibrillation

monitoring: Continuous ECG monitoring for ventricular and supraventricular arrhythmias
Blood pressure and heart rate during loading and infusion
Fluid balance and serum electrolytes, especially potassium
Hemodynamic parameters / cardiac output where available
counsel: This medicine is given by drip in hospital with close heart monitoring
Tell staff if you feel palpitations, chest pain, dizziness, or faintness
Blood pressure, heart rhythm, and kidney function will be checked frequently
The infusion rate may be adjusted based on your response and kidney function
pk: Hemodynamic effects begin within minutes of the loading dose
Peak effect within 5-15 minutes of the loading infusion
Approximately 2.3 hours (prolonged in renal impairment and heart failure)
Effects dissipate within a few hours after stopping the infusion
Store at 15-30 C; protect from light; discard unused diluted solution per protocol
pearls: An 'inodilator' - boosts contractility while lowering preload and afterload
Works independently of beta-receptors, useful in beta-blocked patients
Renally cleared - reduce infusion rate as creatinine clearance falls
Continuous ECG is mandatory because of pro-arrhythmic potential
Do not co-infuse with furosemide (immediate precipitation)
missed: Not applicable - milrinone is administered as a continuous intravenous infusion in a monitored setting by healthcare professionals.
overdose: Overdose may cause hypotension (from vasodilation) and cardiac arrhythmias. There is no specific antidote. Reduce or stop the infusion and provide supportive care, including circulatory support and treatment of arrhythmias and hypotension.
